GMO should definitely not be labeled. Here is a comprehensive, but short, literature review of the topic. The arguments for labeling GMO foods are so poorly constructed that the only possible impact of passing a labeling legislation is a harm on small farmers. Note, must large agribusinesses already grow a sizable organic percentage because it is very profitable. The only group that is reliant on GMO crops are small farms that do not have the monetary ability to transfer into organics. A labeling bill would result in these farmers losing a large percent of their profits while larger businesses can easily make long term changes.

The reason that right to know is not sufficient is that it both does not follow precedent and is the government creating market distortions. A precedent already exists in legal frameworks that the government cannot force businesses to label certain things if it harms the business without consumer benefits. The case example of this is growth hormones. Businesses are not required to put labels on milk or products that use milk from cows that were injected with GH. The reason is that GH milk is equally safe for human consumption when compared to milk from cows that never used GH. Factors like diet, exercise and age are all factors that have been shown to influence milk quality but not GH. We do not label milk based on diet, exercise and age because we homogenize milk and could not conclusively label. This is also true to a lesser extent to GH use. Precedent already exists to suggest since GMO foods are equally safe for consumption then companies do not have to label them.

The government should not be in the businesses of market distortions. The label is meant to force only needed information be provided to consumers. The specific nature of any individual ingredient is left off because they are not a compounding factor. Apple is a very loose botanical term, same with corn or sugar. More specifics could always be used to better address the nature of that crop. However, the average consumer does not know how to reasonably use that information for their own benefit. I know the difference between wheat grown in Montana and New York, but the average consumer does not. It is simply unneeded information. GMO status is simply unneeded information. A more informed choice cannot be made with it on the label because the average consumer does not want to become informed. How many people claim to be all natural without a base understanding of what natural is? It literally means nothing. All natural is a label that any company can use for any product. Companies that want to trick consumers put it on the, or near the, label to get people that will pay more for the same product because the all natural label makes them feel better. A required label must inform the consumer diligently. A label must contain pertinent nutritional information, active ingredients and serving sizes. GMO status is not pertinent because it does not effect that actual product on a consumption level. Banning GMO labels is the correct decision.
